fields.v: A: Execution control harness / LLM Harness DSL (authors' own), version Not stated. B (baseline): GitHub Spec Kit, version Not stated ('standard specification-driven approach')

A: YAML DSL pipeline definition (config + chain of tasks: promptTask, shellTask/checkTask, interactTask; sequential/parallel/iterative/conditional control nodes); prompt files per task with declared input/output scope; system prompt; check definitions (e.g. verify-build); Git commits as checkpoints. B: Spec Kit specification (the 'entire specification, exceeding 100 lines'); other Spec Kit artefacts Not stated

A: Task Scheduler traverses the control tree; each promptTask generates code within an isolated scope, followed by deterministic validation gates (build, static analysis, tests); automatic commit before/after each task; on failure rollback to last valid Git state and fallback to agent or human interaction. In the case study the generation was decomposed into presentation, functional and data tiers. B: whole specification given to the model in one input, followed by iterative manual corrections; Spec Kit phases used Not stated

A: interactTask with control mode R: N -> {auto, human}; fallback_mode 'human' requests human intervention after a failed validation and rollback; review and localized correction by agents or humans. Integration testing and human review remain necessary after the harness. B: manual corrections (65 iterations)
A: full workflow (harness run on one function). B: Spec Kit used with a single specification input (which Spec Kit commands were run is Not stated)
Not classifiable (authors do not use Böckeler's terms; A is an execution-control/harness layer, not a specification format; B described only as a 'specification-driven development tool')

rev.why: The authors place neither approach on an SDD level. A (the harness) is an execution-control layer, so not classifiable fits; but B is GitHub Spec Kit, which Böckeler classifies as spec-first, so a reader classifying by the approaches compared could record B as spec-first (the paper itself gives no detail of how Spec Kit was used).

fields.warn: Os autores não classificam nenhuma abordagem; o harness não é formato de especificação, mas a linha de base é o GitHub Spec Kit (spec-first segundo Böckeler). Decide se classificas pela abordagem proposta ou pelas comparadas.

fields.v: Project: one customer registration function, insurance system ~30 KLOC. Configurations: Spec Kit baseline vs proposed harness. Baseline: GitHub Spec Kit. Held constant: same business requirements, same model (GPT-5) ('identical conditions'); operator, agent, prompts Not stated; baseline had limited prompt tuning. Acceptance tests: Not stated (build/test validation gates in the harness only). Repetitions: 1 per configuration. Human intervention rules: Not stated for the baseline (iterative manual corrections); harness falls back to human on failure

Harness better on all reported dimensions: correction iterations 65 -> 3; development time 9.0 h -> 0.5 h; regressions frequent -> 0; major specification violations observed -> not observed (Table I). No statistical test (single run)

Distinguished the two configurations on all metrics, but single run, single function and model; not repeated. Limitations stated: baseline received limited prompt tuning; iterations and time are proxies for rework cost; single project and model; LLM non-determinism threatens reproducibility

Internal: limited prompt tuning of the Spec Kit baseline; optimized baseline is future work. Construct: correction iterations and time as proxies; finer metrics (code review cycles, defect density) needed. External: single insurance project, one model (GPT-5); other domains and open-source LLMs needed. Non-determinism: validation gates cannot eliminate logical hallucinations; integration testing and human review still needed. Future work: process tailoring with domain knowledge
